{{short description|Theorem in model theory}}
The '''Łoś&ndash;Tarski theorem''', also called the '''Łoś–Tarski preservation theorem''' or '''substructure preservation theorem''', is a result in [[model theory]] that states the [[first-order logic|first-order]] properties are preserved when passing to [[Substructure (mathematics)|substructures]]. It states that a first-order sentence is preserved under substructures if and only if it is logically equivalent to a [[Universal quantification|universal sentence]].<ref>{{citation | first1=Wilfrid | last1=Hodges | author-link=Wilfrid Hodges | title=A Shorter Model Theory | publisher=Cambridge University Press | isbn=0521587131 | year=1997 | page=143}}</ref>

The theorem is named after [[Jerzy Łoś]] and [[Alfred Tarski]]. It is one of the classical preservation theorems of model theory, which relate semantic closure properties of classes of structures to syntactic fragments of first-order logic.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Keisler |first=H. Jerome |title=Some applications of infinitely long formulas |journal=[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]] |volume=30 |issue=3 |year=1965 |pages=339–349 |doi=10.2307/2270580 |jstor=2270580 }}</ref>

== Statement ==

Let <math>T</math> be a theory in a [[first-order|first-order logic]] language <math>L</math> and 
<math>\Phi(\bar{x})</math> a set of formulas of <math>L</math>.
(The sequence of variables <math>\bar{x}</math> need not be
finite.) Then the following are equivalent:
# If <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> are models of <math>T</math>, <math>A \subseteq B</math>, <math>\bar{a}</math> is a sequence of elements of <math>A</math>. If <math>B \models \bigwedge \Phi(\bar{a})</math>, then <math>A \models \bigwedge \Phi(\bar{a})</math>.<br>(<math>\Phi</math> is preserved in substructures for models of <math>T</math>)
# <math>\Phi</math> is equivalent modulo <math>T</math> to a set <math>\Psi(\bar{x})</math> of <math>\forall_1</math> formulas of <math>L</math>.

A formula is <math>\forall_1</math> if and only if it is of the form <math>\forall \bar{x} [\psi(\bar{x})]</math> where <math>\psi(\bar{x})</math> is quantifier-free.

In more common terms, this states that
every first-order formula is preserved under induced substructures if and only if it is <math>\forall_1</math>, i.e. logically equivalent to a first-order universal formula.
As substructures and embeddings are dual notions, this theorem is sometimes stated in its dual form:
every first-order formula is preserved under embeddings on all structures if and only if it is <math>\exists_1</math>, i.e. logically equivalent to a first-order existential formula.
<ref name="Rossman2008">{{cite journal | first1=Benjamin | last1=Rossman |authorlink = Benjamin Rossman| title=Homomorphism Preservation Theorems | journal=[[J. ACM]] | date=2008 | volume=55 | issue=3 | pages=1–53 | url=https://doi.org/10.1145/1379759.1379763 |doi=10.1145/1379759.1379763}}</ref>

A special case is obtained when <math>T</math> is empty, and <math>\Phi</math> contains only a single sentence <math>\varphi</math>. In this case, the theorem states that <math>\varphi</math> is preserved under taking substructures if and only if it is logically equivalent to a universal sentence. Applying this characterization to negations gives the extension-preservation result: that a first order sentence is preserved under extensions if and only if it is logically equivalent to an existential sentence. <ref name="Rossman2008"/>

Note that this property fails for [[finite model theory|finite models]].<ref>{{cite conference
 |last1=Dawar
 |first1=Anuj
 |last2=Sankaran
 |first2=Abhisekh
 |editor-first1=Christel
 |editor-first2=Jean
 |editor-last1=Baier
 |editor-last2=Goubault-Larrecq
 |title=Extension Preservation in the Finite and Prefix Classes of First Order Logic
 |journal=Lipics, Volume 183, CSL 2021
 |series=Leibniz International Proceedings in Informatics
 |year=2021
 |volume=183
 |doi=10.4230/LIPIcs.CSL.2021.18
|doi-access=free
 }}</ref>

== Proof ==

In the usual formulation of the theorem, let <math>\varphi</math> be a first order sentence. Suppose first that <math>\varphi</math> is logically equivalent to the universal sentence <math>\forall \bar{x},\psi(\bar{x})</math>, where <math>\psi</math> is quantifier free. If <math>A\subseteq B</math> and <math>B\models\varphi</math>, then for every tuple <math>\bar{a}</math> of elements of <math>A</math>, <math>B\models\psi(\bar{a})</math>. But quantifier free formulas have the same truth value in a structure and its substructure when evaluated on elements of the substructure, so <math>A\models\psi(\bar{a})</math>. Thus, <math>A\models\varphi</math>. Therefore every universal sentence is preserved under substructures.

Conversely, let <math>\varphi</math> be preserved under substructures. Then, let <math>\Gamma</math> be the set of all universal sentences that logically follow from <math>\varphi</math>. We show that <math>\Gamma\models\varphi</math>.

Let <math>A\models\Gamma</math>. Add a constant symbol for each element of <math>A</math>, and let <math>\operatorname{Diag}(A)</math> be the [[Diagram (mathematical logic)|diagram]] of <math>A</math>, consisting of the atomic and negated atomic sentences true in this expanded structure. The theory

<math display="block">{\varphi}\cup\operatorname{Diag}(A)</math>

is satisfiable. Otherwise, by the [[compactness theorem]], some finite conjunction <math>\delta(\bar{a})</math> of sentences from <math>\operatorname{Diag}(A)</math> would be inconsistent with <math>\varphi</math>. Replacing the new constant symbols in <math>\delta(\bar{a})</math> with variables gives

<math display="block">\varphi\models\forall\bar{x},\neg\delta(\bar{x}).</math>

Since <math>\delta</math> is quantifier free, this is a universal consequence of <math>\varphi</math>, and thus belongs to <math>\Gamma</math>. But <math>A\models\delta(\bar{a})</math>, contradicting <math>A\models\Gamma</math>.

Thus <math>{\varphi}\cup\operatorname{Diag}(A)</math> has a model <math>B</math>. By the diagram lemma, <math>A</math> is isomorphic to a substructure of the reduct of <math>B</math>. Since <math>B\models\varphi</math> and <math>\varphi</math> is preserved under substructures, it follows that <math>A\models\varphi</math>. Thus <math>\Gamma\models\varphi</math>.

By compactness, there is a finite subset <math>\Gamma_0\subseteq\Gamma</math> such that <math>\Gamma_0\models\varphi</math>. By definition of <math>\Gamma</math>, <math>\varphi</math> implies every sentence in <math>\Gamma_0</math>. Therefore

<math display="block">\varphi\equiv\bigwedge\Gamma_0.</math>

A finite conjunction of universal sentences is equivalent to a universal sentence. Thus <math>\varphi</math> is logically equivalent to a universal sentence, completing the converse and proof.<ref>{{cite book |last=Doets |first=Kees |title=Basic Model Theory |publisher=CSLI Publications |year=1996 |isbn=1-57586-048-1 |page=58 |url=https://web.stanford.edu/group/cslipublications/cslipublications/Online/doets-basic-model-theory.pdf
}}</ref>
